extracted.intended_audience: aspiring humor writers, especially those seeking freelance/video work for The Onion / Onion News Network
extracted.subtask_short: writing for The Onion News Network
extracted.subtask_description: Advice and practical expectations for applying as a freelance writer to The Onion (primarily its video/ONN work) and for producing work if hired: packet contents, weekly idea quotas, tone, and what separates successful contributors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application packet: 20 headlines and concepts
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants were required to submit a list of 20 headlines and concepts for video sketches as part of the application packet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This was a core deliverable in the hiring process; the author notes he 'labored over those 20 headlines' and that producing high-quality lists is difficult. Submitters typically emailed resume and samples, received an application, and returned the required list. Anti-pattern: submitting shallow or recycled headlines; do not expect polish to show after staring at ideas too long without fresh angles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application packet: completed script for provided sketch
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants had to complete a script for one of the news segment sketches based on ideas/concepts provided by The Onion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The scripts tested ability to execute a concept into script form; the author notes scripts were hard and prompts were intentionally dry/subtle to test how far you'd take the joke. Emphasize structure, pacing, and ability to expand a dry premise. Scoring notes: staff looked for how you'd turn a brief into a full sketch.

rubrics_metrics.name: High-volume idea generation (quantity requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Writers were expected to produce large quantities of ideas — as a freelancer the author had to turn in 25 ideas a week; during hiring the requirement was 20 headlines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creativity is framed as a muscle: frequent production (many lists, one-liners and sketch concepts) helps get past obvious first ideas and reveals the outlet's voice. Recommendation: prioritize producing volume reliably. Anti-pattern: waiting for one perfect idea rather than producing many iterations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Idea expandability / substance beyond headline
rubrics_metrics.description: An effective idea must be more than a funny sentence; it should have room to be explored and expanded into a 3-minute sketch (substance and potential).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Onion pushed writers to 'see past the headline' — ask whether there's narrative or escalation to sustain a sketch. When submitting, include a short explanation of the joke and how the segment would play out. Anti-pattern: headlines that are funny only as a line with no path to development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Match The Onion's editorial voice (tone and style fit)
rubrics_metrics.description: Writers needed to learn and match The Onion's editorial voice; repetition and producing many pieces helps internalize that voice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Voice-learning occurs through volume and reading approved ideas. When applying, tailor samples and concepts to The Onion's dry, satirical news tone rather than other comedic styles. Scoring guidance: ideas that clearly fit ONN's tone are more likely to be moved forward.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to write both short one-liners and full sketches (format versatility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions and weekly lists contained both one-liners (often used as bottom-screen scrolls) and longer concepts designated for scripting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate versatility by providing a mix of bite-sized jokes and expandable concepts. The staff categorized ideas as 'one liners' or for different show segments; failing to supply both can limit placement opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Take dry/subtle prompts and push them farther (inventiveness with thin prompts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Hiring prompts were often deliberately dry or subtle; evaluators looked for how far applicants would take those modest setups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't rely on flashy premises; show creativity in amplifying a restrained prompt. Example: author notes prompts weren't blockbuster concepts on purpose to test applicants. Anti-pattern: delivering only literal or minimally developed readings of the prompt.

rubrics_metrics.name: No reuse policy / move on from rejected ideas
rubrics_metrics.description: Rejected ideas were considered finished — there was no reuse or iteration on ones that didn't make the cut.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an idea is rejected, focus on new material rather than reworking old lists. This reflects editorial workflow expectations and reduces time wasting. Scoring implication: persistence means producing fresh ideas weekly rather than refining past rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliability, speed, and meeting quotas/deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: The job moved fast and was email-driven; freelancers were expected to meet weekly quotas and deliver on time without in-person meetings or brainstorming.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate ability to work quickly and independently, submit required counts each week (e.g., 25 ideas), and handle remote communication. Anti-pattern: expecting iterative, consultative feedback or collaborative brainstorming sessions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional comedic quality — exceptional levels required for staff positions
rubrics_metrics.description: To become a full-time Onion writer required being 'insanely funny and creative' — strong but not exceptional applicants were unlikely to be hired full-time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author distinguishes being a good writer and matching voice from the rare level of sustained comedic excellence needed for permanent roles. Realistic expectation: freelancing or short stints are possible; full-time roles are highly selective and often require exceptional originality and punch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary hiring pathways: apply persistently, network, or be recruited
rubrics_metrics.description: The author notes current hiring often happens via recruitment, internal promotion (intern/writer's assistant), or knowing someone; unsolicited applications are unlikely to be accepted but occasional job postings appear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advice for applicants: monitor the jobs page, apply when listings appear, be persistent (author applied multiple times), and cultivate industry connections. Anti-pattern: relying solely on a single speculative unsolicited email — chances are low.
